Subject: MSA/Order form — insurance evidence clarification

Irene —

Thanks for sending the order form. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/legal here at TetraTech so we can move to signature:

- Limits: we see the standard limits but need confirmation that commercial general liability is $5M aggregate (per order).
- Additional insured: our legal team needs to be named as additional insured. We prefer the CG 20 10 (or equivalent) endorsement. A COI alone won’t satisfy our contracting group; we need the endorsement language on file.
- Waiver of subrogation: please confirm whether Redwood can provide a waiver in favor of TetraTech where allowed by law.

Can your team route an endorsement request through your broker and share the endorsement PDF (or a carrier-issued endorsement) before countersignature? If timing is tight, confirm what evidence you can provide now and an ETA for the endorsement.

Regards,
Thomas Lee

Irene / team — quick legal review:

- Endorsement form: CG 20 10 is fine; if the carrier issues GL additional insured on a form that contains "primary and non-contributory" we should accept it, but we should avoid language that expands Redwood’s indemnity exposure.
- Waiver of subrogation: we can agree to a waiver where permitted, but carve out — employee theft/fraud and coverages where carrier refuses to waive. I'll draft a short clause for the order form that conditions waiver on carrier acceptance.
- Evidence timing: do not allow countersignature until we have either (i) an issued carrier endorsement or (ii) written broker confirmation with an ETA ≤ 5 business days and a COI showing required limits.

Irene — attached is suggested redline language for the order form insurance section (inline below). We should keep the redline conservative so broker negotiations remain with the insurer.

Suggested: "Seller shall provide an Additional Insured endorsement (CG 20 10 or equivalent) naming Buyer and its affiliates, on a primary and non-contributory basis if reasonably available from Seller's insurer. Any waiver of subrogation shall be conditioned upon carrier acceptance; Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain such waiver."

If Thomas or TetraTech legal wants stricter carrier wording, we should capture that as a contract exception rather than auto-accept.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Waiver of subrogation: generally same — carrier discretion.
- ETA: once we have the executed order form naming details (exact insured name and mailing address), we can typically get carrier review within 48–72 business hours; issuance as a PDF endorsement is usually within 3–7 business days.
